Subject: DPA: proposed legal-hold / backup exception language & e-sign workflow

Hi Peter —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier this week. Attached is our latest DPA with inline redlines (DPA_redlines_v3.pdf). Two items we wanted to surface up front so Orchid's legal team can focus on them: 

1) Backup / DR carve-out: we propose a limited exception that allows retention of encrypted backups for disaster recovery purposes only (no additional analytics or access), with a maximum retention window of 90 days from snapshot creation unless a legal hold is in place. Backups are encrypted with customer-managed keys where requested; access is tightly scoped to our infra team.

2) Preservation / legal-hold: we understand Orchid may need preservation beyond normal deletion schedules for litigation or regulatory requests. Our proposed compromise is a written notice + narrowly scoped preservation period (we propose 60 days after notice) with an audit log of preserved artifacts and monthly review to release holds where possible.

Questions for you / Orchid legal:
- Would Orchid accept 60 days for preservation after written notice (we can add an extendable process tied to court orders)?
- Does Orchid require any special controls for backup encryption or escrow?
- Preferred eSign tool: we typically use DocuSign (link below) but can do AdobeSign if Orchid needs it.

Next steps: if Orchid can review the attached and return counter-redlines or comments, we can have Redwood legal (cc'd) propose final language and produce a sign-ready PDF. I can also set up a 30-min sync next week if that helps.

Thanks Lauren — reviewing now. High-level recommendation and suggested language below (redline-ready):

1) Preservation / legal hold compromise:
- Proposed: "Upon receipt of a written preservation notice specifying the legal basis and scope, Redwood will preserve only those Customer Data reasonably necessary for the identified matter for a period not to exceed sixty (60) days from Redwood's receipt of such notice, unless extended by a court order or mutually agreed in writing. Redwood will provide Customer a monthly status report of preserved data and will release preserved data when no longer reasonably necessary."
- Rationale: 60 days is a common middle ground between our operations needs and their desire for brevity. It also gives time to ingest any formal discovery requests. We can accept 30 days only with a firm clause that Orchid will accept any additional operational risk and manual escalation steps.

2) Backups / DR carve-out:
- Proposed: "Backups taken for disaster recovery will be retained in encrypted form and used solely for restoration and disaster recovery operations. Access to backups will be restricted to personnel with a documented business need and will not be used for product analytics or ad-hoc data access requests. Redwood will delete backup snapshots in accordance with the schedule set forth above unless otherwise required under a preservation notice or court order."
- Add: audit log and attestations quarterly if Orchid requests.

3) eSign workflow:
- We can execute via AdobeSign where required by the counterparty. If Orchid chooses AdobeSign, require recipient authentication (email + phone OTP) and a copy of the executed PDF to be delivered to legal@redwood.com. If DocuSign is used we will provide the DocuSign envelope link for tracking.

Attached is a draft response with the above language ready to send back (redwood_legal_resp_v2.docx). If you want to give Orchid 30 days (their request), we should get explicit acceptance of operational risk and require them to notify Redwood before any preservation notice that intends to be <=30 days so we can prepare.

I can join the call on Fri if needed.
